toolSettingsChangelogText:
`v0.5.1` · 2026-07-28 — Official MCP extension failures are now isolated through lazy connection and full degradation, keeping Sisyphus tools, the CLI, and the outer MCP server available; settings add copy-ready AI setup prompts for MCP and CLI. CLI is now `v0.2.1`.
`v0.5.0` · 2026-07-28 — Official SiYuan MCP ecosystem integration: the new `extension` aggregate tool discovers, filters, and forwards tools registered by other plugins; native SiYuan MCP tools can be enabled separately and remain off by default. CLI is now `v0.2.0`.
`v0.4.15` · 2026-07-23 — Long-document reads now paginate on complete display-block boundaries across `fs` and `document`; file-tree permission badges and quick switching were added, and the settings interface was rebuilt as a consistent responsive workspace. CLI is now `v0.1.18`.
`v0.4.14` · 2026-07-16 — Introduced discoverable MCP scenario Skills and Prompts for browsing, editing, search, databases, exports, tags, flashcards, and system safety, with independently installable CLI/MCP Skill bundles.
`v0.4.8` · 2026-05-24 — Added the feedback tool, manual feedback panel, virtual `/AGENTS.md` workspace memory, and customizable mascot colors, giving agents durable context and a direct product feedback channel.
`v0.4.0` · 2026-05-14 — Launched Document Timeline with named per-document snapshots, visual diff, block or whole-document rollback, and editor integrations; also added self-contained document resource extraction and reorganized settings around permissions and tool groups.
`v0.3.7` · 2026-05-06 — Added the `fs` human-readable path interface (`ls`, `tree`, `read`, `write`, `replace`, `rm`, `mv`, `search`), allowing agents to treat SiYuan documents like Markdown files without learning block IDs or storage paths.
`v0.3.3` · 2026-04-21 — Expanded the standalone CLI with multi-profile `config` management and interactive paging, added MCP/CLI token-cost analytics, and reorganized the bilingual VitePress documentation into task-oriented sections.
`v0.3.0` · 2026-04-18 — Published the first preview of the standalone `siyuan-sisyphus` CLI to npm, exposing the shared aggregate tools through one-shot commands with interactive initialization, schema-aware flags, JSON output, and built-in help.
`v0.2.10` · 2026-04-16 — Unified aggregate-tool definitions through the `defineTool` factory, split the settings UI into focused panels, introduced local analytics and telemetry, and completed end-to-end flashcard creation support.
`v0.2.6` · 2026-04-12 — Made the SiYuan HTTP API configuration file the single source of truth for tool settings, removing local filesystem guessing and aligning plugin, standalone, Docker, and remote deployments.
`v0.2.4` · 2026-04-10 — Removed the plugin-level repository snapshot sidebar because it duplicated SiYuan's official workspace snapshot feature, clarifying the boundary between Sisyphus workflows and native data-history management.
`v0.2.0` · 2026-04-09 — Added stateful Streamable HTTP transport for concurrent MCP clients, plus a settings panel for startup, host, port, Bearer authentication, generated tokens, and copy-ready direct or bridge configurations.
`v0.1.17` · 2026-04-09 — Added the `flashcard` aggregate tool for review, deck, and card operations; rebuilt the bilingual onboarding documentation and expanded the public surface to ten aggregate tools.
`v0.1.9` · 2026-04-03 — Upgraded notebook security to four explicit levels (`none`, `r`, `rw`, `rwd`) and strengthened move, export, server instructions, and permission-aware tool behavior.
`v0.1.5` · 2026-04-02 — Established the aggregate-tool model with notebook, document, block, and file tools; added notebook permission guards, explicit confirmation requirements for dangerous actions, and direct subtree queries.
`v0.1.0` · 2026-02-20 — Established the first public project baseline and introduced the Sisyphus plugin identity with its icon and preview assets.

connectionOverviewDesc: This page provides two connection types: MCP and CLI.
connectionOverviewMcp: MCP: connect SiYuan from MCP-capable clients.
connectionOverviewCli: CLI: run `siyuan-sisyphus` commands directly from a terminal or script.
mcpGuideDesc: Recommended connection methods for different SiYuan installation scenarios.
mcpHttpGuideDesc: Best for desktop direct connections, WSL, LAN access, and cross-machine access. Enabling TLS turns this into HTTPS.
mcpStdioGuideDesc: Best for Docker / remote deployments, or when the client can only launch MCP via stdio.
mcpClientPresetsNote: Choose a client and connection type, then copy the matching format. stdio uses mcp-server.cjs from the current SiYuan plugin directory; HTTP/HTTPS uses the current server URL.
mcpPresetCherryDesc: Copy mcpServers JSON config for Cherry Studio Settings -> MCP Servers.
mcpPresetCcSwitchDesc: Copy CC Switch server-map JSON config.

mcpStdioNote: Note: stdio usually serves one client connection at a time, and it should be preferred for Docker deployments.
mcpAiSetupDesc: Copy a prompt containing the selected client, transport, and exact connection config so a trusted AI can merge and verify it for you.
mcpAiSetupPrompt:
Configure SiYuan Sisyphus MCP in my current AI client.

Target client preset: {{client}}
Transport: {{transport}}

Use this configuration:
```{{format}}
{{config}}
```

You are authorized to inspect and update the current client's MCP configuration. Please:
1. Detect the current OS and the actual configuration file or settings entry used by this client.
2. Read the existing configuration first, merge only the "{{serverName}}" server entry, and preserve all other servers and settings.
3. Treat every token in this prompt as a secret. Do not echo it in logs, summaries, or your final response.
4. For stdio, verify that Node.js and the server script exist. For HTTP/HTTPS, verify that the endpoint is reachable; if the service is stopped, tell me what must be enabled in SiYuan.
5. Reload or reconnect the MCP client as required, then verify the connection by listing tools or calling a harmless read-only action.
6. Report the files or settings changed and the verification result without exposing credentials.

If you cannot edit the client configuration directly, provide the exact target path and commands or UI steps instead.
cliGuideDesc: The CLI connects to SiYuan over the HTTP API directly and does not require the MCP server. Best for terminal, scripts, and automation.
cliGuideInstallDesc: Install the published command-line package globally.
cliGuideInitDesc: Create the local config file with API URL and token.
cliGuideVerifyDesc: Run a simple command to confirm connectivity.
cliGuideHelpDesc: List tools and inspect action help from the terminal.
cliAiSetupDesc: Copy a prompt that authorizes a trusted AI to install the CLI, configure the current SiYuan connection, and verify it.
cliAiSetupPrompt:
Configure the SiYuan Sisyphus CLI in my current environment.

Connection:
- API URL: {{apiUrl}}
- API token: {{apiToken}}
- Profile: default

You are authorized to install or update the published siyuan-sisyphus npm package and update its own CLI configuration. Please:
1. Detect the current OS and confirm that Node.js and npm are available.
2. Install or update siyuan-sisyphus globally.
3. Inspect existing Sisyphus profiles first. Create or update the "default" profile with the API URL and token above, make it active, and preserve unrelated profiles.
4. Treat the token as a secret. Do not echo it in logs, summaries, shell history where avoidable, or your final response.
5. Run read-only verification with "siyuan-sisyphus --version", "siyuan-sisyphus config list", and "siyuan-sisyphus notebook list".
6. Report the installed version, configuration path, active profile, and verification result without exposing the token.

If the API URL is not reachable from the current host, container, WSL, or remote environment, determine the correct route to this SiYuan instance and explain the required adjustment before changing it.
aiSetupSecretWarning: The copied prompt contains connection credentials. Share it only with an AI you trust.
httpUnsupported: HTTP server is only available in the SiYuan desktop app.
httpWarnExposedNoAuth: ⚠️ Bound to a non-loopback address with auth disabled. Other devices on the network can access your SiYuan workspace.

analyticsTokenApproxHint: Approximate token counts based on observed text length; MCP first-connection cost is shown separately from per-call averages.
analyticsRecentCallsHint: Shows the latest 100 local calls with captured input/output text and approximate token counts.

telemetry_enabled_desc: Send aggregated usage statistics to help improve the MCP plugin. No note content, IDs, or paths are ever uploaded.
telemetry_interval_desc: How often to send a telemetry report.
telemetry_endpoint_desc: Optional HTTPS endpoint for aggregated telemetry. Leave empty to disable all telemetry uploads.
telemetryHint: Telemetry sends only aggregated statistics (call counts, error rates, average durations). No note content, IDs, or paths are ever included.
extension_tool_desc: Bridge plugin tools and optionally native SiYuan tools through the official MCP endpoint.
desc_extension_action_list: Inspect the cached official MCP tool registry or refresh it on demand.
extension_discovery_status_desc: Requires SiYuan 3.7.0+, an administrator session, and a valid API token.

extension_include_native_title: Include native SiYuan MCP tools (high risk)
extension_include_native_desc: ⚠️ Security boundary: When enabled, native tools execute with the current SiYuan administrator session or API Token and bypass Sisyphus notebook permissions, disabled actions, and dangerous-action confirmation, so they may read or modify all workspace data accessible to that identity.
